key_insight: A reduced-basis hybrid of Tensor Basis Neural Networks and Universal Differential Equations can learn frame-invariant viscoelastic constitutive laws from shear data and still capture key nonlinear flow behavior in unseen extensional and benchmark flows.
engineering_relevance: This offers a path to digital twins for complex viscoelastic fluids that can be embedded directly into CFD solvers for more physically consistent, data-efficient rheology modeling.
method: Train hybrid TBNN-UDE constitutive models on synthetic oscillatory-shear data from established viscoelastic laws.
Use a reduced tensor-basis formulation to improve physical consistency and numerical stability.
Embed the UDE in an open-source finite-volume solver so stress response is computed dynamically at runtime from local flow conditions.
evidence_signal: The models were trained only on synthetic shear-flow datasets and then evaluated by extrapolation to unseen extensional, 2D, and 3D benchmark flows including 4:1 sudden contraction and cross-slot cases, with accuracy improving when first normal stress difference information was added.
watch_item: Performance degrades as the test flows move further beyond the training regime, so extrapolation to strongly different flow types and high Deborah numbers remains a reliability concern.
paper_title: Harnessing Machine Learning for Hybrid Constitutive Modelling of Viscoelastic Fluid Flows in Computational Rheology
